Subject: Post-call: ShopWise rerank evaluation slate & A/B design

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. High-level recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (5 bullets):
- Primary objective: improve top-10 relevance for category search (mobile + web) while keeping latency impact < 10% at 95th pctl.
- Current baseline: ShopWise production ranker uses TF-IDF + simple learning-to-rank; typical NDCG@10 around 0.32, MRR ~0.27 on the sampled session set you shared.
- Our hypothesis: a two-stage approach (generator -> reranker) with a lightweight candidate reranker can recover relevant items and lift NDCG without significant cost if we use prefix caching + warm KV.
- Quick model suggestions: a distilled cross-encoder quantized to int8 for rerank, and a shortlist generator based on a 7B encoder-decoder for candidate expansion.
- Risks: prompt sensitivity on seasonal SKUs, and ranking regressions on long-tail queries — we'll guard with prompt-level evals and a holdout QA set.

Proposed immediate asks / next steps:
1) Mutual action plan (attached) — review and confirm owners.
2) Share a representative 1M query sample (hashed PKs OK) so we can run a full NDCG/MRR pass.
3) Approve timeline for a 2-week canary A/B: 50k impressions/day initially, then scale if metrics are stable.
4) We will provide: (a) detailed benchmark summary (attached), (b) prompt set v1 for review, (c) suggested metric definitions and alert thresholds.

Attachments: rerank_benchmark_summary.pdf, prompt_set_v1.csv, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Links: Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3ShopWiseEval

If this matches what you expected, confirm the sample transfer and I’ll kick off the dataload and the initial eval run.

Laura / Marissa / Elena — quick technical notes to address the tradeoffs and prompt guardrails Elena asked about.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Distilled cross-encoder (ours): typical NDCG@10 uplift in our pilot customers: +0.04–0.07 absolute with MRR improvements in the same band. P95 latency increase depends on candidate size — with 100 candidates and int8 quantization we measure ~6–9% p95 increase on T4-class hardware; with a 50-candidate rerank path it's ~3–4%.
- Generator + reranker: generator (7B) for candidate expansion tends to add variable latency but can be batched; we recommend running generation asynchronously and caching candidate sets for repeat queries to reduce cost.

Prompt/regression runbook (short):
1) Baseline prompt set v1 (attached) includes targeted templates for cart-intent, navigational, and descriptive queries.
2) For any drop > 1.5% absolute NDCG on a prompt cohort: auto-flag, freeze rollout, and kick-off immediate backfill comparison to last-known-good prompt set.
3) We will instrument per-prompt histograms in the console and wire alerts to PagerDuty for high-severity regressions.

Experiment design notes:
- Split buckets: mobile/cart-intent, mobile/navigational, web/general. We recommend independent scoring so we can avoid masking small but material wins for cart-intent.
- Primary metric: NDCG@10 with secondary MRR and click-through rate (CTR) per bucket.
- Canary cadence: 7-day minimum to stabilize CTR signals; plan for 1-week burn-in, then 2-week observation.

Included: quick benchmark summary (attached) — contains the pilot NDCG / MRR numbers on your sample subset (see top table).

Elena — quick follow-up with concrete plan and asks so we can start the eval next week.

Concrete plan (timeline):
- Day 0–3: data ingest + hashing validation (ShopWise infra to share 1M sample).
- Day 4–7: run full NDCG/MRR pass across prompt cohorts (we will attach per-prompt breakdown).
- Day 8–14: deploy reranker to canary buckets (mobile/cart-intent + web/general), 50k impressions/day target, monitoring dashboards live.
- Day 15–28: scale canary to 25% traffic if no major regressions; final decision gate at day 28.

A/B design specifics:
- Buckets: mobile/cart-intent (primary), mobile/navigational (safety), web/general (overflow).
- Metrics: primary = NDCG@10 (cart-intent), secondary = MRR, CTR (safety).
- Guardrails: immediate rollback on >1.5% absolute NDCG drop in any safety bucket or CTR drop >2% on navigational.

Next asks for ShopWise:
1) Confirm sample export and ownership (we'll need S3 read access or temporary GCS link).
2) Confirm mobile p95 latency budget number so we can calibrate candidate size.
3) Approve the mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) — I included owner suggestions and due dates.

We’ll stand up the first eval run as soon as Step 1 is complete. Happy to sync again for 15 minutes tomorrow if you want to walk through the plan.
